subject: Commercials: pricing ladder, invoice split, net30 & VAT handling
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan@skyline.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Order form & billing model questions after demo

Ben — thanks again for the demo this morning. Skyline's procurement team asked for a straighter view of the commercial mechanics before we proceed: a clear pricing ladder for the commit tiers, how minimum commits are invoiced (phased vs up-front), and whether Redwood can support invoices split between our US entity and our EU subsidiary (reverse-charge / VAT).

High-level asks:
- We prefer Net30 across the board if possible.
- We need invoices split: some invoices paid by Skyline AI Inc. (US) and some by Skyline AI EU GmbH.
- If Redwood needs to collect VAT, do you gross-up price or will our EU entity self-assess via reverse-charge?

Can you circulate a sample order form and the typical sequencing for tranche invoices? Data security and MSA redlines are OK on our side but commercial sequencing is the blocker.

Thanks — Evan
Evan Brooks
Director, Partnerships | Skyline AI
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan@skyline.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-15T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form & billing model questions after demo

Evan — appreciate the clarity. I've attached a draft order form (Skyline_OrderForm_v1.pdf) showing the pricing ladder and a recommended phasing tied to commit bands. Quick notes:
- Draft assumes 3-tier commit ladder with automatic step-up pricing at each band.
- Default billing in the draft is 50% upfront per tranche and 50% invoiced over the following 30 days (can adjust).
- We typically list taxes as a separate line item; collection approach depends on billing entity and tax residency.

Two clarifying Qs so we can finalize:
1) Which entity will sign the order form? (we need invoice remit details and a PO if you use one)
2) For the EU split — do you have an existing VAT certificate for Skyline EU, or do you want Redwood to invoice gross and remit VAT?

Looping Hannah (commercials) and Laura (finance) so they see the ask. I'll hold final until legal/finance weigh in.

Attachment: Skyline_OrderForm_v1.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Evan Brooks <evan@skyline.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-16T08:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form & billing model questions after demo

Ben — quick answers:
- Signatory will be Skyline AI Inc. (US) for the master order we intend to execute. We will provide a PO for the initial tranche.
- For the EU split, Skyline AI EU GmbH will handle VAT; we can provide VAT registration details. We were hoping Redwood could support splitting invoices so the EU subsidiary receives the invoice lines for EU usage and can self-assess (reverse-charge).
- Net30 is preferred.

If Redwood needs to invoice gross for any reason, we can discuss a gross-up clause but would prefer to avoid extra fees — the ask is really for proper invoice routing and clear tax treatment.

Evan
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T10:11:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Redlines - Order form tax & invoicing approach (Skyline)

Team — I reviewed the draft Order Form Ben attached and sketched redlines (see Redlines_v1.docx). Key proposed positions for commercial/legal consistency: 

1) Invoice sequencing & minimum commits
- Keep the 3-tier pricing ladder, but link invoicing triggers to commit thresholds (we invoice on achievement of the tranche trigger rather than purely time-based). This reduces our credit exposure.

2) Net terms
- Accept Net30 for customer-facing invoices. Add a clause that failure to provide required PO/VAT evidence within 10 business days converts remaining invoices to Net0 until evidence provided (operational protection).

3) Split invoicing & tax handling
- We can accommodate split invoices to different legal entities, but require: billing entity and remit-to details for each tranche at signing; a signed billing addendum; and a VAT registration certificate for the EU entity pre-commencement.
- Preferred approach: Redwood invoices US entity for US-tiered usage; Redwood invoices EU entity for EU-tiered usage. For cross-border services where VAT is ambiguous, Redwood will list taxes separately and the customer will self-assess where legally applicable.
- Gross-up: avoid automatic gross-up. If customer requires gross-up, charge an administrative fee of 1.5% on invoiced amounts and add a clause to the Order Form.

4) Attachments / evidence
- Request Finance (Laura) to confirm the operational PO flow and whether Skyline requires consolidated invoicing for accounting consolidation.

I recommend we present this as an options list to Evan: (A) Redwood invoices gross and remits VAT (rare — requires EU onboarding); (B) Split invoices with customer-provided VAT certs (preferred); (C) Split invoices + gross-up at 1.5% (if customer cannot provide certs).

I've included line edits in Redlines_v1.docx and flagged specific clause numbers in the MSA. Happy to walk through on a quick call if helpful.

Attachment: Redlines_v1.docx (docx)

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan@skyline.ai>, Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-22T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form & billing model questions after demo — proposed commercial approach

Evan / Patricia — thanks for the quick responses and patience while we reviewed internally. Below is a concise proposed commercial compromise to keep the deal moving without looping legal each time: 

Summary (what Redwood proposes)
- Pricing ladder: keep the 3-tier commit bands as in the attached Order Form. Each tranche has a clear commit trigger.
- Invoicing sequencing: invoice at tranche trigger. For each tranche we will issue two invoices by default: a 50% invoice at trigger and a follow-up invoice for the remaining 50% within Net30. If you prefer a single invoice per tranche we can update.
- Net terms: Net30 on all customer-facing invoices. If Skyline does not provide required PO/VAT evidence within 10 business days of signature, future tranche invoices will be suspended until evidence is provided (operational safeguard).
- Split invoicing / VAT: Redwood can route invoice lines to both Skyline AI Inc. (US) and Skyline AI EU GmbH. We require the EU VAT registration certificate and remit-to details for the EU entity at signing. For ambiguous cross-border services Redwood will list VAT as a separate line; customer may self-assess under reverse-charge.
- Gross-up: Redwood's baseline position is no automatic gross-up. If Skyline needs Redwood to invoice gross and remit VAT, we can do so but will include a 1.5% administrative charge and a short EU onboarding checklist.

Next steps
1) Ben to provide an updated Order Form that incorporates the billing addendum for entity split and the Net30/10-business-day evidence clause.
2) Evan to confirm the exact billing remit details and provide a VAT certificate for Skyline EU.
3) Laura to confirm PO routing and internal account code we should reference on invoices.

I've attached the current draft order form with Kim's redlines for your review (Skyline_OrderForm_v1.pdf, Redlines_v1.docx). If this high-level approach works for you, Ben will redline the order form and we can move to signature + PO.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Commercials | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Skyline_OrderForm_v1.pdf, Redlines_v1.docx
